blocks.content: The Director of CBI has been provided security of tenure in office for a period of two years in terms of the provisions of the Central Vigilance Commission Act, 2003.

rows: CVC, Vigilance Commissioners, Secretaries from MHA and DoPT
Prime Minister, Leader of Opposition (Lok Sabha), and CJI / SC Judge
Mandatory inclusion of LoP or Leader of Single Largest Opposition Party

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Director of CBI is appointed as the head of the organization responsible for the overall administration of the agency.
The Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013 amended the Delhi Special Police Establishment (DSPE) Act, 1946, changing the composition of the selection committee.
The appointment committee consists of the Prime Minister (Chairperson), the Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha, and the Chief Justice of India or a Supreme Court Judge nominated by him.
In the absence of a recognized Leader of Opposition, the leader of the single largest opposition party in the Lok Sabha is included in the selection committee.
The Director of CBI is provided a minimum guaranteed tenure of two years under the provisions of the Central Vigilance Commission (CVC) Act, 2003.
The CBI Director selection committee is chaired by the Prime Minister, NOT the Home Minister or the Central Vigilance Commissioner.
If there is no official Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha, the Leader of the Single Largest Opposition Party is mandatory in the selection panel.
The statutory 2-year tenure security was instituted following the Supreme Court's ruling in the landmark Vineet Narain Case (1997).
